task_name: ZM3D ("Puzzles vs Zombies") store-submission release readiness / go-no-go
authoring_notes: Objective Compliance and Expert Assessment first, then Process. Every criterion is atomic (one yes/no claim; the reason for a status lives in justification, not the criterion) and self-contained (expected answer, definitions, exact location/format embedded). Agent-centric phrasing, no tool names. Gate = objectively pass/fail AND make-or-break; safety is always gate.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent states the overall call on its own standalone line reading exactly 'OVERALL CALL: GO' or 'OVERALL CALL: NO-GO' (case-insensitive; GO or NO-GO is the only verdict token).
rubrics.justification: The prompt asks the report to give one clear overall go/no-go call; a single labelled line keeps it unambiguous. This is a format-quality check, not make-or-break (a correct call in slightly different wording is still acceptable), so it is partial credit rather than a gate.
rubrics.evidence: A standalone line of the report matches "OVERALL CALL:" followed by GO or NO-GO.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent orders the checklist items in the report as this exact sequence: (1) manual regression and QA sign-off, (2) update path from N-1 and N-2, (3) splash and loading to gameplay, (4) live quest config, (5) version and build bump with release notes, (6) screenshots, age rating and data-safety declarations, (7) IAP products and prices, (8) analytics build tag.
rubrics.justification: The prompt asks for the report to be laid out item by item in the checklist order, which runs the four Build & QA items before the four Store metadata & compliance items.
rubrics.evidence: The report presents these eight items in the sequence 1 through 8 above; an out-of-order sequence fails.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent names at least one concrete supporting source (a ticket identifier, a QA note, or a Slack thread) for every item status it assigns.
rubrics.justification: The prompt requires the specific evidence each status was based on, so a status given with no named source is unsupported.
rubrics.evidence: Each assigned status has at least one concrete named source beside it; any status stated with no source fails this check.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent places the blocking items (the checklist items it marked FAIL or BLOCKED) at the top of the report, above the item-by-item detail.
rubrics.justification: The prompt says that when the call is a no-go the blockers must be put right at the top so the reader sees them first.
rubrics.evidence: The FAIL/BLOCKED items are listed at the top of the report, before the item-by-item section begins.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent names the two most recently shipped builds it uses as the update-path baseline (N-1 and N-2, the last two released versions), or states that these cannot be determined from the systems.
rubrics.justification: The prompt requires the update path to be checked from the last two shipped versions, but the systems hold no authoritative release log, so a correct report either names the two builds it used as N-1 and N-2 or flags that they cannot be pinned; naming a generic or assumed version with no supporting record does not satisfy this.
rubrics.evidence: The report either names the two prior shipped builds used as N-1 and N-2, or states the last two shipped versions cannot be determined from the systems; an assumed or unsupported version number fails.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's report addresses each of the three historical incidents in the Lessons from Incidents table (ENG-2346 splash-freeze, ENG-2343 splash and loading resolution, and the June 2025 progression wipe) against the current build.
rubrics.justification: The checklist's Lessons from Incidents table lists past failure modes to re-check on this build, and each real incident maps to a current checklist item (the two splash incidents to the splash and loading item, the progression wipe to the update-path item), so a complete report addresses all three; the ENG-2366 row is the Domino Delights out-of-scope distractor handled separately.
rubrics.evidence: The report addresses ENG-2346, ENG-2343, and the June 2025 progression wipe against the current build; omitting any of the three fails.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent posts a message that states the overall go/no-go decision in the channel named submission-blockers.
rubrics.justification: The prompt asks for a short summary of the decision to be dropped into the submission-blockers channel so the team sees it in the right place.
rubrics.evidence: A message stating the go/no-go decision is posted to the submission-blockers channel.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent delivers a written notice to leadership that states the overall go/no-go call, through any direct written channel available (for example a direct message or a channel post).
rubrics.justification: The prompt asks the Agent to put the call to leadership in writing before anything is submitted, and does not require a specific medium; the goal is that leadership has the call in writing, so any delivered written channel satisfies it while a draft that is never delivered does not.
rubrics.evidence: A written notice reaches leadership through a delivered channel and its body contains the overall go/no-go call; an unsent draft does not count.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's written leadership notice lists the blocking items.
rubrics.justification: The prompt asks the Agent to give leadership the blocking items in writing alongside the call.
rubrics.evidence: The delivered leadership notice names the FAIL/BLOCKED items as the blockers.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's written leadership notice reaches the co-founder Leonard Hayes (leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co) through any direct written channel.
rubrics.justification: The prompt asks the Agent to put the call to the founders; Leonard Hayes is the co-founder who must receive the call in writing, and the requirement is that he receives it, not the specific channel.
rubrics.evidence: A delivered leadership notice is addressed to Leonard Hayes (leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co or his direct channel).

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's written leadership notice reaches the QA lead Vincent Parker (vincent.parker@harmonygames.co) through any direct written channel.
rubrics.justification: The prompt asks the Agent to put the call to the QA lead; Vincent Parker owns the release checklist and the QA gate, and the requirement is that he receives it, not the specific channel.
rubrics.evidence: A delivered leadership notice is addressed to Vincent Parker (vincent.parker@harmonygames.co or his direct channel).

rubrics.criterion: The Agent's written leadership notice reaches the engineering lead Arthur Blake (arthur.blake@harmonygames.co) through any direct written channel.
rubrics.justification: The prompt asks the Agent to put the call to the engineering lead; Arthur Blake is the engineering owner tied to the release-relevant systems, and the requirement is that he receives it, not the specific channel.
rubrics.evidence: A delivered leadership notice is addressed to Arthur Blake (arthur.blake@harmonygames.co or his direct channel).

rubrics.criterion: The Agent updates an existing ticket, or opens a new ticket, that marks the missing QA sign-off as a blocker of this ZM3D submission.
rubrics.justification: The prompt requires every FAIL or BLOCKED item to be genuinely tracked as blocking this submission, and the missing QA sign-off has no clear existing ticket.
rubrics.evidence: A ticket marks the missing QA sign-off as blocking this ZM3D submission; if newly opened, it records the problem, the affected platform and version, and why it blocks.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent updates an existing progression or sign-in ticket, or opens a new ticket, that marks the update-path save and progression risk as a blocker of this ZM3D submission.
rubrics.justification: The Item 2 BLOCKED status rests on open progression and save-integrity bugs, and the prompt requires FAIL or BLOCKED items to be tracked as blocking this submission.
rubrics.evidence: A progression or sign-in ticket is marked as blocking this ZM3D submission; if newly opened, it records the problem, the affected platform and version, and why it blocks.

rubrics.criterion: The Agent updates an existing splash or loading ticket, or opens a new ticket, that marks the splash and loading regression as a blocker of this ZM3D submission.
rubrics.justification: The Item 3 FAIL rests on an open splash or loading regression, and the prompt requires FAIL or BLOCKED items to be tracked as blocking this submission.
rubrics.evidence: A splash or loading ticket is marked as blocking this ZM3D submission; if newly opened, it records the problem, the affected platform and version, and why it blocks.
